Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
17 October 2026 .
Brent $ 109.86 + 3.72 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 Al Jazeera and the Straits Times report Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport, with the Saudi-led coalition intercepting a separate missile headed for Yanbu.

02 Iranian state media, including Mehr News and IRNA, claim a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude caught fire after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz; no maritime authority has confirmed the incident.

03 Brent settled at $109.86, up 3.72% in the last session before the close; WTI stood at $101.41.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains closed to commercial traffic, with the feed's 60 headlines in the past 24 hours reflecting sustained pressure across both the strait and the wider region. The most operationally significant development outside the strait: Al Jazeera and the Straits Times report that Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport, with the Saudi-led coalition intercepting a missile headed for Yanbu. Inside the strait, Iranian state media continue to assert mine activity. Mehr News and IRNA claim a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude caught fire and exploded after striking a naval mine; aol.co.uk and WANA News Agency carry the same report. No maritime authority has confirmed the incident. Moneycontrol reports 15 Indian crew aboard oil tanker MT ST 3 are safe after the vessel was hit by a projectile. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent settled at $109.86, up 3.72% in the last session before the close; WTI stood at $101.41. Iran's position, per its army spokesman as covered in the background, is that the strait reopens only if the United States leaves the region; US Central Command continues to assert it controls the waterway. As of 06:22 UTC, 150 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
